items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...like Lester Lannan, say, and they just take a whole bunch of tunes...

ctx.x: Well, when anybody would ask for a roll-a-long little dogey, they used to get sick. They'd say, oh no. I'd put it in the metal and get rid of it quickly. You know what I mean? I'd call it something else, and then when I'd finish up with it, because I don't know how many people throw buns at me, you know what I mean? But there wasn't a bad tune.

Did you used to connect the tunes to some of the Society orchestras today? They just, they start a beat up, like Lester Lannan, say, and they just take a whole bunch of tunes, they have it all rehearsed and everything, and they go from one thing to the other with just a little kind of an interlude- Modulation. Modulation, or, and change you out a little bit so that people don't get bored with the same key. Yeah. And then they keep going on for a long time like that. Did you used to play a tune and stop and start…

Well, no. We would play an arrangement on a tune. It was only the hackney tunes. I mean, the tunes that were so well known, we'd play from one to the other. We'd play a medley. And if it was the tune that we didn't care too much about, we'd put it in a medley. See? And we used to play mostly waltz medleys. Unless like, oh, like when you want to sign off, you might want to sign off for the waltz. To Night Sweetheart or something? Yeah, well I had a medley, but the bands used to call Steal It.
